messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Numeric integration
parts:
I don't think we're going to be supporting Fortran linkage
any time soon --- we have enough build headaches as it is.

The simplest thing to do would probably to get a boost
integrator, then just autodiff it to start and make sure
you get reasonable results, then do the analytic derivatives.

Then we can go looking for better integrators, etc. when
the analytic bits are sorted out.

- Bob

On Monday, November 30, 2015 at 6:15:08 PM UTC-5, Marco Inacio wrote:
Why not the one Ben Goodrich suggested? It's C++ and seems pretty
simple. Also, I couldn't find boost numerical integrator.

Boost doesn't have a general numerical integrator. I think it would be difficult to expose a function like integrate() into the Stan language because no single numerical integration procedure works well on every problem. But Cook's approach works well on functions that decline at a double exponential rate, which covers a lot of things one might want to do in statistics. So, I think something like this could be included in Stan Math and used when appropriate as the back end by functions exposed to the Stan language.

Ben

is called --- think of it as forming a scope just like
in a program.
